title: Partner Technical & Commercial Onboarding Guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document is a combined technical and commercial onboarding guide for platform partners (ISVs, channel partners, and system integrators). It codifies the minimal requirements, SLOs, integration steps, and commercial checkpoints required to move a partner from initial engagement to production launch on Redwood Inference. The goal is to standardize the experience so partners meet performance/compliance expectations while minimizing engineering hand-hold time.

Audience:
- Partner engineering managers and integration engineers
- Redwood partner managers and solutions engineers
- Sales and legal teams finalizing commercial terms

Goals:
- Deliver a repeatable 8-week onboarding path for non-enterprise partners and a configurable 12–16 week path for enterprise integrations.
- Ensure measurable performance: 95th percentile latency <= 250ms for transactional routes in hosted mode (see SLOs).
- Validate commercial readiness: billing setup, SKU mapping, crediting and contract sign-off.

Scope and partner types:
- ISVs integrating Redwood API directly into a product (primary focus).
- Channel partners white-labeling Redwood-powered features.
- System integrators deploying Redwood Private for regulated customers.

Required preconditions (check before kickoff):
1) Signed NDA and partner intake form completed by partner manager.
2) Partner has a technical contact and schedule for weekly syncs.
3) Billing entity exists or a purchase order path is identified (finance).
4) For Private deployments: network reachability test and customer KMS details available.

Ownership matrix:
| Activity | Redwood owner | Partner owner | Escalation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Technical integration (API keys, test creds) | Partner Solutions (eng) | Partner engineering lead | Partner manager -> AM
| SLO validation & perf testing | Eng-Platform (Benchmarking) | Partner QA | SRE oncall
| Contract & billing | Finance & Sales Ops | Partner procurement | Legal
| Security review & data handling | Security & Compliance | Partner security lead | Security director

Key SLOs and thresholds (integration stage vs. post-launch):
- Integration stage (verification tests):
  - 95th percentile tail latency for test suite (end-to-end): <= 350ms
  - Error rate during synthetic load tests: < 0.5%
- Production SLOs (post-launch):
  - 95th percentile request latency: <= 250ms (transactional routes)
  - Uptime: 99.9% monthly for hosted integrations; Dedicated SLA will be contract-specific
  - Token cost variance: observed unit cost within +/-15% of projected estimate in the first 30 days

Onboarding flow (8–16 week template):
1) Kickoff (week 0) — kickoff deck, success criteria, communication channels.
2) Discovery (week 0–1) — traffic profile, peak QPS, typical sequence length, and privacy constraints.
3) Sandbox integration (week 1–3) — partner implements requests against Redwood sandbox API keys; sample test suite executed.
4) Performance validation (week 3–4) — run perf harness (see Commands) and adjust batching/kv caching settings.
5) Commercial finalize (week 4–5) — SKU mapping, billing method, early-consumption credit if applicable.
6) Security & compliance review (parallel, week 2–6) — SOC/pen test checklist and data residency confirmation.
7) Canary launch (week 5–8) — 1–5% traffic, monitor SLOs, escalate on regression.
8) Production rollout (week 8+) — phased traffic increase with rollback gates.

Technical integration checklist:
- API credentials: obtain partner sandbox key and production key.
- Model selection: confirm model variant(s) (e.g., redwood-rlhf-7b-q4f) and fallback variants.
- Batching strategy: sample batch_size and max_latency tradeoffs documented.
- KV/prefix cache: identify session prefixes for caching and TTLs.
- Observability: configure per-route telemetry in Console; enable traces and token-level cost snapshots.
- Webhooks & tooling: configure event webhooks for usage alerts and quota notifications.

Perf harness (commands):
- Synthetic runner (example):
  ./perf-runner --target https://sandbox.api.redwood.ai/generate \n    --key REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY \n    --concurrency 50 --rps 300 --duration 300 --sequence-distribution profiles/short-medium.json

- Sample cURL for a streaming conversational route:
  curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_KEY}" -X POST \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-3b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the quarterly results."}],"stream":true}' \n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions

Commercial and billing checklist:
- SKU mapping: map partner features to Redwood SKU(s). Typical mapping examples included in appendix.
- Discounting: determine early-adopter credits and overage rate tiers.
- Entitlements: confirm which routes are included in the base SKU vs. paid add-ons (e.g., dedicated warm capacity).
- Quota setup: set soft quotas for first 30 days with alerting at 70%/90%.

Security & compliance checkpoints:
- Data handling: confirm PII/no-PII policy and whether request/response logging is permitted for evals.
- Access control: RBAC role assignments for partner SREs (read-only by default).
- Audit logging: ensure audit logs forwarded to partner or partner-managed SIEM if required.
- Private deployment specifics: KMS integration test, HSM handshake, network peering checklist.

Canary and rollback gates (operational criteria):
- Canary metrics evaluated every 30 minutes for 24 hours: latency, error rate, token cost per minute.
- Automatic rollback triggers: sustained 95th percentile latency above SLO for 30 minutes, or error rate >1% for 15 minutes.
- Manual rollback: Partner requests immediate rollback via support channel; SRE executes session evacuation plan.

Go-live checklist (must be green):
- All integration tests passing in production keys.
- Billing entity active and invoice test completed.
- SLO dashboard created and subscribed for alerts.
- Security sign-off completed.
- Runbook created and shared with partner for first 72 hours post-launch.

Post-onboarding: metrics & cadence:
- Weekly health sync for first 4 weeks; then biweekly for 2 months; monthly thereafter until business metrics stabilize.
- Reported metrics: per-route latency, per-tenant token cost, quota burn rate, incidents and degradations.
- Quarterly business review: consumption vs. forecast and fidelity adjustments.

Templates and artifacts (links to internal templates):
- Kickoff deck template: confluence://templates/partner-kickoff-deck
- Integration test suite: git://infra/partner-integration-tests (see README)
- Billing SKU template: confluence://templates/partner-sku-mapping

Appendix A — Example SLA lines (sample text for inclusion in partner contract):
- Redwood will provide hosted inference availability of 99.9% measured monthly. Credits are applied when availability falls below the threshold: 5% credit for 99.0–99.9%, 15% for 98.0–99.0%.
- SLO for transactional 95th percentile latency: 250ms. Measured for endpoints designated as "transactional" in the onboarding form.

Appendix B — Example SKU mapping (sample):
| Feature | Redwood SKU | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Chat API (up to 4k tokens) | sku-chat-std | Base entitlement in Starter plan
| Chat API (up to 32k tokens) | sku-chat-large | Add-on for enterprise-grade sessions
| Dedicated warm capacity | sku-dedicated-warm-1 | Monthly reserved GPU pool

Appendix C — Troubleshooting quick commands:
- Dump active sessions for tenant:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_KEY}" https://console.redwood.ai/v1/admin/tenants/${TENANT_ID}/sessions\n
- Force-evacuate sessions for a canary rollback:
  ./evacuate-sessions --tenant ${TENANT_ID} --grace-period 30 --dry-run=false

Contact and escalation list:
- Partner Solutions (primary): solutions-partners@redwood.ai, on-call: +1-555-0123
- Benchmarking & Performance: perf-eng@redwood.ai
- Commercial & Billing: partner-billing@redwood.ai
- Security & Compliance: secops@redwood.ai
